questions.q: In AKS, which part of the cluster does Azure manage on Northbridge's behalf?
options: Nothing — AKS only provides VMs, the customer runs everything
The control plane: the API server, etcd, and scheduler
The application code running inside Pods
Only the virtual network, not Kubernetes itself
questions.explain: AKS's defining feature is that Azure runs and patches the control plane (API server, etcd, scheduler) for free; the customer still manages the node pools.

questions.q: Why would Northbridge add a separate user node pool instead of running everything in the default system node pool?
options: A user node pool is required before any Pod can be scheduled
So application Pods (checkout, catalog) aren't competing with core cluster components for the same nodes, and each pool can be sized or scaled independently
System node pools cannot run any Pods at all
User node pools are free while system node pools are billed
questions.explain: Separating a user node pool from the system node pool keeps application workloads from contending with cluster-critical system components, and lets each be managed on its own terms.

questions.q: Once `kubectl` is connected to an AKS cluster via kubeconfig, how does working with it differ from a self-managed cluster covered earlier in this course?
options: Every kubectl command needs an --aks flag
It doesn't differ for day-to-day kubectl usage — Deployments, Services, RBAC, etc. all work the same way against AKS
AKS clusters cannot run Deployments, only Pods
kubectl must be replaced entirely with the az CLI
questions.explain: AKS is still standard Kubernetes underneath; once kubeconfig points at it, everything taught earlier in the course (workloads, networking, RBAC, etc.) applies unchanged.

questions.q: What is the main reason Northbridge specifically chose AKS rather than self-hosting Kubernetes's control plane on its own Azure VMs?
options: AKS is the only option that supports Linux containers
Self-managing the control plane is real ongoing operational work (patching, backups, availability) that AKS offloads to Azure, and Northbridge already runs other services on Azure
Self-hosted Kubernetes clusters cannot use persistent storage
AKS does not require any node management at all
questions.explain: The lesson frames AKS's value as removing the operational burden of running the control plane yourself, which fits naturally for a team already committed to Azure.
